meta.title: Sentence Court: Combining for Effect

questions.prompt: The cyclist checked the map. She adjusted her route. Which sentence combines the ideas with an introductory present participial phrase?
choices: While checking the map, the route was adjusted by the cyclist.
Checking the map, her route was adjusted.
Checked the map, the cyclist adjusted her route.
Checking the map, the cyclist adjusted her route.
questions.explanation: The present participial phrase Checking the map logically modifies the main subject, the cyclist.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Merge the sentences with a present participial phrase that shows the storm caused the valley to be covered: The snowstorm continued through the night. The valley was buried in snow.
choices: The snowstorm continued through the night, it buried the valley in snow.
The snowstorm continued through the night, burying the valley in snow.
The snowstorm continued through the night because burying the valley in snow.
The snowstorm, continuing through the night buried the valley in snow.
questions.explanation: The present participial phrase burying the valley in snow modifies The snowstorm and shows that the storm caused the snow to cover the valley.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The coach explained the drill. She demonstrated each movement. Which combined version preserves parallel verb forms?
choices: The coach explained the drill and was demonstrating each movement.
The coach explained the drill and demonstrated each movement.
The coach explained the drill and to demonstrate each movement.
The coach explaining the drill and demonstrated each movement.
questions.explanation: The coordinated verbs explained and demonstrated are parallel in form and share the subject The coach.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The outdoor movie will start at dusk. The forecast calls for scattered showers. Choose the version that uses even if to show that the showers will not stop the movie.
choices: The outdoor movie will start at dusk only if the forecast calls for scattered showers.
The forecast calls for scattered showers even if the outdoor movie will start at dusk.
The outdoor movie will start even if the forecast calls for scattered showers at dusk.
The outdoor movie will start at dusk even if the forecast calls for scattered showers.
questions.explanation: The even if clause makes scattered showers a condition that will not prevent the movie from starting at dusk.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with concessive even if
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The path narrowed near the cliff. After noticing it, we slowed our pace. Which option combines the ideas with an after clause and gives the correct one-sentence explanation?
choices: After the path narrowed near the cliff, we slowed our pace. The after clause identifies the reason for slowing our pace.
After we slowed our pace, we noticed that the path narrowed near the cliff. The after clause identifies the reason for slowing our pace.
After noticing that the path narrowed near the cliff, we slowed our pace. The after clause establishes the sequence between noticing the narrowing and slowing down.
After noticing that the path narrowed near the cliff, we slowed our pace. The after clause joins two independent clauses.
questions.explanation: The after clause establishes the sequence between noticing that the path had narrowed and slowing the pace.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The student wrote the essay. The essay received an award. Which combined sentence uses a restrictive relative clause to identify the student?
choices: The student, who wrote the essay, received an award.
The student who wrote the essay received an award.
The essay that the student wrote received an award.
The student who wrote an essay received an award.
questions.explanation: The clause who wrote the essay restricts the reference to the specific student who wrote that essay.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The reporter interviewed the mayor. She hoped to verify the budget figures. Which sentence uses a simple infinitive phrase of purpose without an introductory preposition?
choices: The reporter interviewed the mayor in order to verify the budget figures.
The reporter interviewed the mayor to verify the budget figures.
The reporter interviewed the mayor to verified the budget figures.
The reporter interviewed the mayor for verify the budget figures.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to verify the budget figures states the purpose of the interview without an introductory preposition.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The trail was flooded. We turned back early. Which sentence combines the ideas by using because to make the flooding the cause of our decision?
choices: Although the trail was flooded, we turned back early.
Because we turned back early, the trail was flooded.
Because the trail was flooded, we turned back early.
While the trail was flooded, we turned back early.
questions.explanation: Because the trail was flooded introduces the reason we turned back early and places the cause before the result.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a causal clause
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The judges will announce the winner tonight. They will contact the runners first. Which version uses subject-auxiliary inversion in both independent clauses?
choices: Will the judges announce the winner tonight, and the judges will contact the runners first.
Will the judges announcing the winner tonight, and will they contact the runners first.
Will the judges announce the winner tonight and they will contact the runners first.
Will the judges announce the winner tonight, and will they contact the runners first?
questions.explanation: The correct version inverts the subject and auxiliary in both clauses: will the judges announce and will they contact.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The porch light began to flicker. We continued reading on the couch. Combine the sentences so that both actions happen at the same time, using a while clause.
choices: While the porch light began to flicker, we continued reading on the couch.
Although the porch light began to flicker, we continued reading on the couch.
Because the porch light began to flicker, we continued reading on the couch.
If the porch light began to flicker, we continued reading on the couch.
questions.explanation: The while clause places the flickering porch light and the continued reading in the same time frame.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a temporal while clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The library will close at six. Visitors must return books before then. Which sentence joins the ideas with a colon that introduces the additional requirement?
choices: The library will close at six; visitors must return books before then.
The library will close at six, and visitors must return books before then.
The library will close at six: visitors must return books before then.
The library will close at six, so visitors must return books before then.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the second independent clause, which states the additional requirement about returning books.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The power failed during the storm. The clinic kept treating patients. Which sentence combines the ideas with despite followed by a gerund phrase?
choices: Despite the clinic kept treating patients, the power failed during the storm.
Despite of the power failing during the storm, the clinic kept treating patients.
Despite the power failed during the storm, the clinic kept treating patients.
Despite the power failing during the storm, the clinic kept treating patients.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase the power failing follows despite correctly and preserves the contrast between the outage and the clinic's continued work.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The wind tore a branch from an old oak. The branch crashed onto the toolshed. Which sentence combines the ideas into a balanced compound sentence with parallel past-tense verbs?
choices: The wind tore a branch from an old oak while the branch crashed onto the toolshed.
The wind tore a branch from an old oak, and the branch crashed onto the toolshed.
The wind tore a branch from an old oak, and the branch was crashing onto the toolshed.
The wind tore a branch from an old oak because the branch crashed onto the toolshed.
questions.explanation: The sentence is a balanced compound because it joins two independent clauses, the wind tore and the branch crashed, with parallel past-tense verbs.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The trail was icy. The hikers continued carefully. Which sentence combines the ideas with a concessive clause using although?
choices: Although the trail was icy, but the hikers continued carefully.
Although the trail was icy; the hikers continued carefully.
Although the trail was icy the hikers continued very carefully.
Although the trail was icy, the hikers continued carefully.
questions.explanation: The concessive although clause shows that the hikers continued carefully despite the icy trail.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The archivist will unlock the archive. The researchers can begin their work after that. Which sentence uses subject-auxiliary inversion to make unlocking the archive the condition for the researchers beginning their work?
choices: After the archivist unlocks the archive, the researchers can only begin their work.
Only after the researchers can begin their work will the archivist unlock the archive.
Only after the archivist unlocked the archive could the researchers begin their work.
Only after the archivist unlocks the archive can the researchers begin their work.
questions.explanation: The inverted structure can the researchers begin places the main clause after the fronted only after-clause, which states the condition.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The teacher asked the class to compare the maps. The students discussed the differences in pairs. Rewrite the pair with so that to show the comparison as the purpose of the teacher's request.
choices: The teacher asked the class to compare the maps because the students could discuss the differences in pairs.
The teacher asked the class to compare the maps unless the students could discuss the differences in pairs.
The teacher asked the class to compare the maps so that the students could discuss the differences in pairs.
The teacher asked the class to compare the maps although the students could discuss the differences in pairs.
questions.explanation: The so that clause presents comparing the maps as the purpose of the teacher's request.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a purpose clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The lights flickered. The room went quiet. Which sentence combines the ideas with as to show the first action continuing as the second occurred?
choices: As the lights flickered, the room went quiet.
Because the lights flickered, the room went quiet.
Although the lights flickered, the room went quiet.
Before the lights flickered, the room went quiet.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses as to place the flickering lights and the room becoming quiet on the same timeline while presenting the lights as the established event.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The guide will explain the map. The guide will not collect the tickets. Which sentence combines the ideas using neither...nor with parallel verb forms?
choices: The guide neither explain the map nor will collect the tickets.
The guide will neither explain the map nor collecting the tickets.
The guide will neither explain the map nor collect the tickets.
The guide will neither explain the map or collect the tickets.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly pairs neither with nor and uses the parallel base forms explain and collect after the shared modal verb will.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The robotics club began its presentation. The room was crowded with visitors. Which sentence combines the ideas with despite followed by a noun phrase?
choices: Despite of the crowded room, the robotics club began its presentation.
Despite the crowded room, the robotics club began its presentation.
Despite the room being crowded, the robotics club began its presentation.
In spite of the crowded room, the robotics club began its presentation.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase the crowded room follows despite directly and makes the contrast between the crowded setting and the presentation's beginning clear.
questions.skill: Using a preposition with a noun phrase
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentences with a nonrestrictive relative clause that adds information about Ms. Chen: Ms. Chen is our biology teacher. She has won two national awards.
choices: Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, is our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, was our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, whose two national awards she has won, is our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, are our biology teacher.
questions.explanation: The nonrestrictive relative clause who has won two national awards supplies extra information about Ms. Chen without restricting the reference to one specific teacher.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Why does the sentence Although the bus was delayed, the team reached the final on time, count as a complex sentence?
choices: It contains one dependent Although-clause and one independent main clause.
It joins two independent main clauses with the coordinating conjunction but.
It pairs a present participial phrase with an independent main clause.
It uses one dependent because-clause with an independent main clause.
questions.explanation: The sentence has one independent main clause and the dependent Although the bus was delayed clause, which is the defining structure of a complex sentence.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The evidence was confusing. The jury asked for clarification. Which sentence combines the ideas with a correct so...that result clause?
choices: The evidence was so confusing the jury asked for clarification.
The evidence was confusing so that the jury asked for clarification.
The evidence was such confusing that the jury asked for clarification.
The evidence was so confusing that the jury asked for clarification.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence places the intensifier so before the adjective and includes that to introduce the result.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Maya is our project manager. She will lead the planning team. Which sentence combines the ideas with a nonrestrictive appositive?
choices: Maya, our project manager, will lead the planning team.
Maya who is our project manager will lead the planning team.
Being our project manager, Maya will lead the planning team.
The project manager will lead the planning team, and Maya is that person.
questions.explanation: Our project manager is a nonrestrictive appositive that renames Maya while adding information about her role.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The warning bell rang. Everyone stopped talking. Which sentence combines the ideas with the traditional no sooner...than construction and a past perfect auxiliary?
choices: No sooner did the warning bell ring than everyone stopped talking.
No sooner had the warning bell rung than everyone stopped talking.
No sooner had the warning bell rang than everyone stopped talking.
No sooner had the warning bell rung when everyone stopped talking.
questions.explanation: The traditional construction places had after no sooner and uses the past participle rung in the first clause.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The audience had barely sat down. The lights suddenly went out. Which sentence combines the ideas with a correct hardly...when inversion?
choices: Hardly had the audience sat down, the lights suddenly went out.
Barely the audience had sat down when the lights suddenly went out.
Hardly had the audience sat down when the lights suddenly went out.
Hardly had the audience sat down the lights suddenly went out.
questions.explanation: The correct construction places had before the subject and uses when to introduce the unexpected second event.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The lighthouse stands on a rocky bluff. It is called the North Point Light. Which sentence combines the two ideas with an appositive?
choices: The lighthouse which is called the North Point Light stands on a rocky bluff.
The lighthouse, called the North Point Light stands on a rocky bluff.
The lighthouse, called the North Point Light, stands on a rocky bluff.
The lighthouse stands on a rocky bluff, called the North Point Light.
questions.explanation: The phrase called the North Point Light is an appositive that renames the lighthouse while adding identifying information.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a cumulative structure, adding layers of detail to a basic description?
choices: The field was green although it was dotted with yellow flowers, and a low stone wall bordered it.
The field was green because it was dotted with yellow flowers, and a low stone wall bordered it.
The field was green, dotted with yellow flowers, and bordered by a low stone wall.
The field was green; it was dotted with yellow flowers, and a low stone wall bordered it.
questions.explanation: The successive participial phrases expand the initial description of the field in a cumulative sequence.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The outdoor class was postponed. The schoolyard was covered in mud. Which sentence combines the ideas using because of followed by a noun phrase?
choices: The outdoor class was postponed because of cover the schoolyard in mud.
The outdoor class was postponed because of the schoolyard was covered in mud.
The outdoor class was postponed because of the muddy schoolyard.
The outdoor class was postponed because of muddy the schoolyard.
questions.explanation: The phrase because of the muddy schoolyard gives the reason for postponing the class in the required noun-phrase form.
questions.skill: Combining ideas with because of and a noun phrase
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The drummer practices percussion. She also plays the synthesizer. Which sentence combines the ideas with as well as and parallel verb forms?
choices: The drummer practices percussion as well as the synthesizer is played.
The drummer practices percussion as well as play the synthesizer.
The drummer practices percussion as well as played the synthesizer.
The drummer practices percussion as well as plays the synthesizer.
questions.explanation: The sentence preserves the two present-tense activities with the parallel verbs practices and plays.
questions.skill: Combining ideas with as well as and parallel verbs
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Join the sentences with a causal clause that explains why the instructions were easy to read: The instructions were printed in bold. They were easy to read.
choices: The instructions, because they were printed in bold, was easy to read.
The instructions were printed in bold because they were easy to read.
The instructions being printed in bold, they were easy to read.
The instructions were easy to read because they were printed in bold.
questions.explanation: Because introduces a causal clause that correctly explains why the instructions were easy to read.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The volunteers collected supplies. They loaded them into the van. Which sentence combines the ideas with a present participial phrase?
choices: The volunteers collected supplies, the van loaded with them.
The volunteers collected supplies, loading them into the van.
The volunteers collected supplies, loaded them into the van.
The volunteers collected supplies, and loaded them into the van.
questions.explanation: The present participial phrase loading them into the van describes an action performed by the volunteers.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Create a complex sentence that makes early opening the condition for the tour time: The museum may open early. The tour will begin at eight.
choices: If the museum opens early, the tour will begin at eight.
The museum may open early, and the tour will begin at eight.
Although the museum opens early, the tour will begin at eight.
The museum may open early, the tour will begin at eight.
questions.explanation: The if-clause makes early opening the condition under which the eight o'clock tour will begin.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The committee will not approve the proposal. It will not announce the winner yet. Which sentence combines the ideas with neither...nor and parallel verb forms?
choices: The committee will neither approve the proposal nor announce the winner yet.
The committee will neither approve the proposal nor announcing the winner yet.
The committee will neither approves the proposal nor announce the winner yet.
The committee will neither approve the proposal nor the winner will be announced yet.
questions.explanation: Using neither...nor with approve and announce keeps both verbs in the same future-tense form and clearly negates both actions.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The hikers chose the marked trail. They did not follow the unmarked shortcut. Rewrite the pair using rather than followed by the base form of follow.
choices: The hikers chose the marked trail rather than follows the unmarked shortcut.
The hikers chose the marked trail rather than follow the unmarked shortcut.
The hikers chose the marked trail rather than following the unmarked shortcut.
The hikers chose the marked trail and rather than following the unmarked shortcut.
questions.explanation: The bare infinitive follow parallels the main verb chose and preserves the contrast between choosing the marked trail and rejecting the shortcut.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with rather than and parallel verbs
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The choir rehearsed in the auditorium. The drama club painted scenery in the basement. Show the different activities of the two groups with a whereas clause.
choices: The choir rehearsed in the auditorium, whereas the drama club painted scenery in the basement.
The choir rehearsed in the auditorium, because the drama club painted scenery in the basement.
The choir rehearsed in the auditorium, and the drama club painted scenery in the basement.
The choir rehearsed in the auditorium, while the drama club painted scenery in the basement.
questions.explanation: The whereas clause contrasts the choir's rehearsal with the drama club's scenery painting.
questions.skill: Contrasting ideas with a whereas clause
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The lake froze. The skaters would not go onto it. Which combined sentence makes the freezing a condition for the skaters' decision?
choices: Unless the lake froze, the skaters would not go onto it.
Because the lake froze, the skaters would not go onto it.
The lake froze; the skaters would not go onto it.
If the lake froze, the skaters would not go onto it.
questions.explanation: An if clause makes the lake's freezing the condition for the skaters staying off the ice.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The coach reviewed the play. The coach noticed an inconsistency. Which sentence combines the ideas with an introductory present participial phrase whose implied subject is the coach?
choices: Reviewing the play, an inconsistency was noticed by the coach.
The coach, reviewing the play, noticed an inconsistency.
While reviewing the play, the coach noticed an inconsistency.
Reviewing the play, the coach noticed an inconsistency.
questions.explanation: Reviewing the play is a present participial phrase that modifies the coach and introduces the main clause without using a subject.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The archivist delivered a folder. The folder contained duplicate prints. Which sentence uses a restrictive relative clause to identify the folder?
choices: The archivist delivered the folder that had contained duplicate prints.
The archivist delivered the folder whom had contained duplicate prints.
The archivist delivered the folder, which contained duplicate prints.
The archivist delivered the folder that were containing duplicate prints.
questions.explanation: The clause that had contained duplicate prints restricts the reference to one specific folder and provides the information needed to identify it.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The chef reviewed the data. The chef found an error. Which combined sentence begins with a present participial phrase rather than a prepositional or subordinate clause?
choices: Reviewing the data, the chef found an error.
While reviewing the data, the chef found an error.
After reviewing the data, the chef found an error.
Before reviewing the data, the chef found an error.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase Reviewing the data is a present participial phrase whose understood subject is the chef.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The researcher checked the data twice. The data were complete. Which sentence combines the ideas with the coordinating conjunction and joining two independent clauses?
choices: The researcher checked the data twice because the data were complete.
The researcher checked the data twice, and the data were complete.
The researcher checked the data twice, whereas the data were complete.
The researcher checked the data twice, for the data were complete.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the coordinating conjunction and to join two independent clauses, each of which can stand alone as a complete sentence.
questions.skill: Joining independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The printer stopped. The staff saved their documents. Which sentence combines the ideas with while to show that the two events happened at the same time?
choices: Because the printer stopped, the staff saved their documents.
While the printer stopped, the staff saved their documents.
Although the printer stopped, the staff saved their documents.
If the printer stopped, the staff saved their documents.
questions.explanation: While the printer stopped presents the printer stopping and the staff saving their documents as simultaneous events.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a while clause
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The package was fragile. The courier handled it with extra care. Which sentence combines the ideas with a grammatically correct not only...but also construction?
choices: Not only was the package fragile, but the courier also handled it with extra care.
Not only the package was fragile, but the courier also handled it with extra care.
The package was not only fragile, but the courier also handled it with extra care.
Not only was the package fragile, but the courier handled it with extra care also.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence uses fronted not only with inversion and places also after the second subject.
questions.topic: Activity 3 of 9 (quiz/game): Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence combines the two ideas as a compound sentence joined by a semicolon?
choices: Her explanation was clear, so the students understood the lesson.
After her explanation was clear, the students understood the lesson.
Her explanation was clear; the students understood the lesson.
Her explanation was clear, and the students understood the lesson.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses—her explanation was clear and the students understood the lesson—without creating a comma splice.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The sun set. We began the night hike. Which sentence uses once to show that the hike began immediately after sunset?
choices: Unless the sun set, we began the night hike.
Until the sun set, we began the night hike.
Once the sun set, we began the night hike.
Since the sun set, we began the night hike.
questions.explanation: Once the sun set means that the night hike began immediately after the sun had set.
questions.skill: Combining sentences with a once clause
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The wind might rise. The race will be postponed. Which sentence expresses the condition with an inverted conditional clause beginning with Should?
choices: Should the wind rise, the race will be postponed.
If the wind should rise, the race will be postponed.
Should the wind will rise, the race will be postponed.
The wind should rise, the race will be postponed.
questions.explanation: Beginning the conditional clause with Should places the subject before the verb and expresses the condition without using if.
questions.topic: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The road will remain open. We can finish the hike safely. Which sentence correctly expresses that finishing the hike safely depends on the road remaining open?
choices: Only if the road will remain open can we finish the hike safely.
Only if the road remains open can we finish the hike safely.
Only when the road remains open, we can finish the hike safely.
If the road remains open, only can we finish the hike safely.
questions.explanation: The correct version places the conditional clause first and correctly inverts the subject and helping verb to express only if.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The gardener pruned the hedge. She discovered a bird's nest inside it. Which sentence combines the ideas with an introductory present participial phrase whose implied subject matches the main-clause subject?
choices: While pruning the hedge, the gardener discovered a bird's nest inside it.
Having pruned the hedge, the bird's nest was discovered inside it.
Pruning the hedge, a bird's nest was discovered by the gardener.
Pruning the hedge, the gardener discovered a bird's nest inside it.
questions.explanation: The introductory participial phrase Pruning the hedge has an implied subject of the gardener, who performs both the pruning and the discovery.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The students entered the gym. Their shoes were soaked from the puddle. Which sentence combines the ideas with an absolute phrase?
choices: The students entered the gym, their shoes soaked from the puddle.
The students entered the gym, soaking their shoes from the puddle.
The students entered the gym with their shoes soaked from the puddle.
The students entered the gym, their shoes were soaked from the puddle.
questions.explanation: The clause their shoes soaked from the puddle is an absolute phrase that adds information about the students without becoming a separate sentence.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Nora will submit the report online. She will bring it to the office. Which sentence combines the ideas with either...or, one subject, and parallel predicates?
choices: Either Nora will submit the report online or she will bring it to the office.
Nora will either submit the report online, or bring it to the office.
Nora will either submit the report online or bring it to the office.
Nora will neither submit the report online nor bring it to the office.
questions.explanation: This version uses either...or with the single subject Nora and the parallel predicates submit and bring.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The workshop teaches note-taking. The workshop provides practice. Choose the sentence that uses a both...and construction with parallel verb forms.
choices: The workshop both teach note-taking and provides practice.
The workshop both teaches note-taking and provides practice.
The workshop both teaches note-taking and provide practice.
The workshop teaches note-taking and both provides practice.
questions.explanation: The both...and construction coordinates the parallel verbs teaches and provides while making the workshop the single subject.
questions.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Rewrite the sentences with a nonrestrictive relative clause that adds information about Ms. Chen: Ms. Chen is our biology teacher. She has won two national awards.
choices: Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, is our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, was our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, whose two national awards she has won, is our biology teacher.
Ms. Chen, who has won two national awards, are our biology teacher.
kept.explanation: The nonrestrictive relative clause who has won two national awards supplies extra information about Ms. Chen without restricting the reference to one specific teacher.
kept.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Merge the sentences with a present participial phrase that shows the storm caused the valley to be covered: The snowstorm continued through the night. The valley was buried in snow.
choices: The snowstorm continued through the night, it buried the valley in snow.
The snowstorm continued through the night, burying the valley in snow.
The snowstorm continued through the night because burying the valley in snow.
The snowstorm, continuing through the night buried the valley in snow.
kept.explanation: The present participial phrase burying the valley in snow modifies The snowstorm and shows that the storm caused the snow to cover the valley.
kept.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which sentence combines the two ideas as a compound sentence joined by a semicolon?
choices: Her explanation was clear, so the students understood the lesson.
After her explanation was clear, the students understood the lesson.
Her explanation was clear, and the students understood the lesson.
Her explanation was clear; the students understood the lesson.
kept.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses—her explanation was clear and the students understood the lesson—without creating a comma splice.
kept.topic: Combine Two Sentences - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Join the sentences with a causal clause that explains why the instructions were easy to read: The instructions were printed in bold. They were easy to read.
choices: The instructions, because they were printed in bold, was easy to read.
